summary: The promoted action adapter retained a robust factual-video SSIM gain but did not improve every action-sensitive metric, so the action-control interpretation and SOTA claim remain rejected.
evidence: Official and promoted checkpoints each completed 4 factual/swapped clip pairs at seeds 42, 314159, and 20260811 with identical 57-frame, 9-history-frame, 20-step budgets.
Clips were grouped into two physical wipe_table episodes; seeds were averaged before the 10,000-iteration paired bootstrap.
Future SSIM improved from 0.823330 to 0.829861 with oriented gain 0.006531 and lower bound 0.003742.
Flow endpoint error slightly regressed from 2.066107 to 2.067347 pixels; its oriented-gain lower bound was -0.001580.
Wrong-action SSIM-margin and flow-margin lower bounds were -0.001428 and -0.005080, so neither action-sensitivity gain was established.
The audit was decision-ineligible because only two independent physical episodes were available versus the frozen minimum of 20.
lessons: The current adapter improves factual reconstruction quality but available evidence does not show that the gain comes from stronger causal use of EEF trajectories.
Action-counterfactual and lineage gates catch claims that pixel-fidelity promotion alone cannot support.
BWM eef_abs must be described as realized absolute EEF trajectory conditioning rather than low-level command control.
limitations: The suite contains one task, one embodiment, one camera rig, and two independent physical episodes.
No physical counterfactual rollout exists, so swapped-action quality is diagnostic rather than causal ground truth.
No contact, collision, task-success, or real-robot evidence was collected.
next_actions: Expand to at least 20 independent resets with executable paired counterfactuals, then train against a preregistered action-causal objective rather than SSIM alone.
Do not promote the current adapter as improved action control unless every primary causal and non-regression gate passes.
